short_description.id: Ame no Hiwashi adalah dewa dalam mitologi Jepang, leluhur klan Inbe di Awa yang membuka Provinsi Awa, menanam serat, dan merintis pemintalan; kini dipuja sebagai Otori-sama.
short_description.en: Ame no Hiwashi is a deity in Japanese mythology, ancestor of the Inbe clan of Awa who opened up Awa Province, planted fibres and founded spinning work; today he is worshipped as Otori-sama.

long_description.id: Ame no Hiwashi (天日鷲神) adalah dewa dalam mitologi Jepang yang muncul dalam Nihon Shoki dan Kogo shūi. Ia dianggap leluhur klan Inbe di Awa dan dikreditkan membuka Provinsi Awa, menanam serat, dan merintis pemintalan. Ia juga disebut Oe no Kami dan Inbe no Kami; Ensiklopedia Shinto menyebutnya anak Tajikarao, sedangkan sumber lain menyebutnya keturunan Takamimusubi atau Kamimusubi.
long_description.en: Ame no Hiwashi (天日鷲神) is a deity in Japanese mythology who appears in the Nihon Shoki and the Kogo shūi. He is regarded as the ancestor of the Awa Inbe clan and credited with opening up Awa Province, planting fibres and founding spinning work. He is also called Oe no Kami and Inbe no Kami; the Encyclopedia of Shinto calls him a child of Tajikarao, while another source calls him a descendant of Takamimusubi or Kamimusubi.

long_description.id: Saat Amaterasu bersembunyi di gua batu surga dan pada turunnya cucu langit, ia dikatakan menanam murbei kertas dan membuat persembahan serat kulit kayu (nigite), sehingga dipandang sebagai kami pekerjaan untuk perkakas ritual. Dalam mitos terkenal, ia memainkan alat petik dan seekor elang hinggap di senarnya, sehingga aksara elang ditambahkan pada namanya.
long_description.en: At the time of Amaterasu's hiding in the heavenly rock cave and at the descent of the heavenly grandchild, he is said to have planted paper mulberry and made bark-fibre offerings (nigite), so he is considered an occupational kami of ritual implements. In the well-known myth he played a stringed instrument and an eagle perched on its string, so the character for eagle was added to his name.

long_description.id: Keturunannya menyeberang ke Awa di Shikoku mencari tanah untuk biji-bijian dan rami, dan klan Inbe Awa mempersembahkan tekstil rami dan murbei kertas kepada kaisar pada Daijōsai; keluarga Miki, yang dianggap keturunan Inbe Awa, menyiapkan aratae pada penobatan. Ia dikenal sebagai Otori-sama dan dipuja sebagai dewa pelindung hasil tangkapan, perdagangan dan industri, serta nasib baik; kuil utamanya antara lain Washi Jinja di Tokyo dan Inbe Jinja di Tokushima.
long_description.en: His descendants crossed to Awa in Shikoku seeking land for grains and hemp, and the Awa Inbe clan offered hemp and paper-mulberry textiles to the emperor at the Daijōsai; the Miki family, regarded as descendants of the Awa Inbe, prepares the aratae at accessions. He is known as Otori-sama and worshipped as a guardian of catches, commerce and industry, and good fortune; his principal shrines include Washi Shrine in Tokyo and Inbe Shrine in Tokushima.

cultural_context.id: Sebagai kami pekerjaan, ia dikaitkan dengan pembuatan perkakas ritual, pemintalan, dan pembuatan kertas, dan keturunannya mempersembahkan tekstil kepada kaisar pada Daijōsai; kini ia dikenal sebagai Otori-sama.
cultural_context.en: As an occupational kami he is linked to ritual implements, spinning and papermaking, and his descendants offer textiles to the emperor at the Daijōsai; today he is known as Otori-sama.

statement.en: In the well-known myth, when Amaterasu entered the heavenly rock cave and the gods began to dance, Ame no Hiwashi played a stringed instrument and an eagle perched on the end of the string; the gods rejoiced at it as an auspicious bird, and the character for "eagle" (washi) was added to his name.

statement.id: Menurut Kogo shūi, ia salah satu dari empat dewa pengikut Futodama; ketika Amaterasu bersembunyi di gua batu, ia menanam kajinoki dan kapas serta membuat nigite putih, sehingga disebut "dewa penanam rami" dan menjadi dewa pemintalan dan pembuatan kertas.
statement.en: According to the Kogo shūi, he is one of four deities following Futodama; when Amaterasu hid in the rock cave he planted paper mulberry and cotton and made white nigite, so he is also called the "hemp-planting kami" and becomes a kami of spinning and papermaking.

short_description.id: Amilamia adalah peri baik hati mitologi Basque dari Agurain, Alava, berambut emas yang tinggal di gua Lezao dan menolong orang miskin.
short_description.en: Amilamia is a kindly fairy of Basque mythology from Agurain, Alava, with golden hair, who lives in the Lezao cave and helps the poor.

long_description.id: Amilamia adalah makhluk gaib baik hati mitologi Basque dari daerah Agurain di Alava, yang menurut tradisi tinggal di gua Lezao di pegunungan Entzia. Ia perempuan berambut pirang seperti emas yang menjuntai sampai tanah; ia menyisirnya dengan sisir emas di tepi kolam gua sambil bernyanyi dalam bahasa tak dikenal. Ia punya ayakan ajaib yang menghasilkan tepung walau kosong dan menolong orang miskin serta gembala.
long_description.en: Amilamia is a benevolent supernatural being of Basque mythology from the Agurain area of Alava who by tradition lived in the Lezao cave in the Entzia range. She is a woman with golden-blond hair reaching the ground, which she combs with a golden comb by the cave pool while singing in an unknown tongue. She had a magic sieve that made flour though empty, and helped the poor and shepherds.

long_description.id: Federico Baraibar dan José Miguel de Barandiaran mencatat Amilamia sebagai nama lamia di Agurain, dan Pemerintah Basque menyebutnya salah satu nama daerah untuk lamiak. Ia varian lamiak yang lebih lembut; sebagian legenda menyebutnya satu tokoh, yang lain satu jenis roh.
long_description.en: Federico Baraibar and José Miguel de Barandiaran record Amilamia as the name of a lamia at Agurain, and the Basque Government lists it among regional names for the lamiak. She is a gentler variant of the lamiak; some legends make her one figure, others a kind of spirit.

short_description.id: Ampelos adalah satir muda, personifikasi pohon anggur, kekasih Dionysus yang menurut berbagai kisah diubah menjadi pohon anggur atau rasi bintang.
short_description.en: Ampelos is a young satyr, a personification of the grapevine and lover of Dionysus, who in various accounts became the grapevine or a constellation.

long_description.id: Ampelos adalah personifikasi pohon anggur dan kekasih Dionysus (Bacchus), seorang satir. Menurut Theoi, ia satir muda dari Thrakia yang tampan, dan menurut Fasti karya Ovidius ia putra seorang nimfa dan seorang satir yang dicintai Bacchus.
long_description.en: Ampelos was a personification of the grapevine and lover of Dionysus (Bacchus), a satyr. According to Theoi he was a handsome young Thrakian satyr, and according to Ovid's Fasti he was the son of a nymph and a satyr whom Bacchus loved.

long_description.id: Ada beberapa kisah tentang akhir hidupnya. Menurut Theoi, dalam satu kisah ia dibunuh banteng liar dan diubah menjadi pohon anggur pertama, dalam kisah lain ia jatuh dari pohon elm saat memetik anggur dan menjadi rasi bintang. Menurut Wikipedia, Dionysus mengubahnya menjadi rasi bintang atau pohon anggur, dan menurut Nonnus ia tewas ditanduk banteng liar setelah mengejek dewi Selene.
long_description.en: There are several accounts of his end. According to Theoi, in one he was slain by a wild bull and became the first grapevine, in the other he fell from an elm tree while picking grapes and became a constellation. According to Wikipedia, Dionysus turned him into a constellation or the grapevine, and according to Nonnus a wild bull gored him to death after he mocked the goddess Selene.

long_description.id: Dalam Dionysiaca karya Nonnus, Ampelos menunggang banteng dan menantang Selene, "aku bertanduk dan aku menunggang banteng"; Selene yang cemburu mengirim lalat pengejar ternak sehingga banteng itu berlari liar. Dalam Fasti karya Ovidius, Ampelos jatuh saat memetik anggur dan Liber mengangkatnya ke bintang-bintang.
long_description.en: In Nonnus' Dionysiaca, Ampelos rode a bull and challenged Selene, "I have horns and I ride a bull"; the jealous Selene sent a cattle-chasing gadfly so that the bull galloped off wildly. In Ovid's Fasti, Ampelos fell while picking grapes and Liber lifted him to the stars.

short_description.id: Andromalius adalah iblis dalam demonologi Eropa. Menurut Goetia ia berpangkat earl, tampil sebagai manusia yang memegang ular, dan bertugas menangkap pencuri serta mengembalikan barang curian.
short_description.en: Andromalius is a demon in European demonology. According to the Goetia he is an earl who appears as a man holding a serpent and whose office is to bring back thieves and stolen goods.

long_description.id: Andromalius adalah iblis dalam demonologi Eropa. Dalam Goetia ia menempati urutan ke-72, berpangkat earl yang besar dan perkasa, dan memimpin 36 legiun roh.
long_description.en: Andromalius is a demon in European demonology. In the Goetia he is the 72nd spirit, a great and mighty earl, who rules 36 legions of spirits.

long_description.id: Goetia melukiskan bahwa ia tampil dalam bentuk manusia yang memegang ular besar. Tugasnya membawa kembali pencuri beserta barang curian, menyingkap kejahatan dan tindakan curang, menghukum pencuri dan orang jahat lain, serta menemukan harta yang tersembunyi.
long_description.en: The Goetia describes him appearing in the form of a man holding a great serpent. His office is to bring back a thief and the stolen goods, to discover wickedness and underhand dealing, to punish thieves and other wicked people, and to discover hidden treasure.

long_description.id: Ia tidak muncul dalam Pseudomonarchia Daemonum. Penyunting Goetia mencatat bahwa namanya sering muncul dalam mantra mandiri di naskah sihir dengan ejaan seperti Andromalcus, untuk menemukan pencuri atau harta. Dalam okultisme populer Jepang, 江口之隆 menduga ia dahulu dewa pencuri Kanaan; ini dugaan penulis modern, bukan tradisi kuno.
long_description.en: He does not appear in the Pseudomonarchia Daemonum. The Goetia's editor notes that his name often appears in stand-alone spells in magic manuscripts, with spellings such as Andromalcus, for detecting a thief or discovering treasure. In Japanese popular occultism 江口之隆 speculates that he was once a Canaanite god of thieves; this is a modern writer's conjecture, not an ancient tradition.

long_description.id: Ao (鰲, juga ditulis 鼇) adalah kura-kura laut besar dalam mitologi Tiongkok. Ia dianggap pernah hidup di Laut Tiongkok Selatan pada masa pembentukan dunia. Menurut kamus Kangxi yang mengutip Shuowen, ao adalah kura-kura besar di laut.
long_description.en: Ao (鰲, also written 鼇) is a huge sea turtle of Chinese mythology, thought to have dwelt in the South China Sea when the world was taking shape. The Kangxi Dictionary, citing the Shuowen, defines the ao as a great turtle of the sea.

long_description.id: Ketika dewi Nüwa memperbaiki langit setelah bencana, ia memotong keempat kaki Ao dan memakainya sebagai penyangga. Terjemahan Liezi oleh Giles mencatat bahwa Nüwa memotong kaki Ao untuk menyangga empat sudut langit, dan Giles menyebut makhluk ini "Atlas" Tiongkok, yaitu penyu laut raksasa. Kamus Kangxi yang mengutip Sanhuang Benji juga menyebut Nüwa memotong kaki ao untuk menegakkan empat tiang.
long_description.en: While the goddess Nüwa was mending the sky after a catastrophe, she cut off the four legs of Ao and used them as props. Giles's translation of the Liezi likewise has her cut off the legs of the Ao to hold up the four corners of the heavens, and Giles calls the creature a Chinese "Atlas", a gigantic sea-turtle. The Kangxi Dictionary, quoting the Sanhuang Benji, says as well that Nüwa cut off the ao's feet to set up the four poles.

long_description.id: Mitos lain menyebut Ao masih hidup di Laut Bohai dan memikul tiga pulau milik delapan dewa abadi (Penglai, Fangzhang, dan Yingzhou) di punggungnya; Yupian yang dikutip kamus Kangxi menyebut ao yang bergaib memikul gunung Penglai di laut. Ao dianggap memengaruhi sosok naga-kura-kura Bixi dalam seni pahat Tiongkok kekaisaran. Nama tempat yang memuat ao lebih khas di pesisir tenggara Tiongkok.
long_description.en: A different myth says Ao is still alive in the Bohai Sea, bearing on its back the three islands of the Eight Immortals (Penglai, Fangzhang and Yingzhou); the Yupian, quoted in the Kangxi Dictionary, speaks of a divine ao carrying Mount Penglai in the sea. Ao is thought to have shaped the later dragon-and-turtle figure Bixi in imperial Chinese sculpture. Place names containing ao are typical of the southeastern coast of China.

statement.id: Kamus Kangxi mengutip Shuowen bahwa ao (鼇) adalah kura-kura besar di laut; Yupian menyebut ao yang bergaib memikul gunung Penglai di punggungnya di laut; dan Sanhuang Benji menyebut Nüwa memotong kaki ao untuk menegakkan empat tiang. Kamus ini menilai penulisan 鰲 sebagai bentuk umum yang tidak tepat.
statement.en: The Kangxi Dictionary quotes the Shuowen that the ao (鼇) is a great turtle in the sea; the Yupian that a divine ao carries Mount Penglai on its back in the sea; and the Sanhuang Benji that Nüwa cut off the ao's feet to set up the four poles. The dictionary regards the writing 鰲 as a popular but incorrect form.

short_description.id: Ao Ao adalah monster rakus mirip domba bertaring, putra terkutuk Tau dan Kerana dalam mitologi Guarani.
short_description.en: Ao Ao is a voracious, fanged sheep-like monster, a cursed son of Tau and Kerana in Guarani mythology.

long_description.id: Ao Ao adalah makhluk mengerikan dari mitologi Amerika Selatan, salah satu putra terkutuk Tau dan Kerana dan salah satu makhluk mitologi utama dalam budaya berbahasa Guarani. Sebuah sumber museum di Paraguay menyebutnya putra keenam Tau dan Kerana. Ia sering digambarkan sebagai makhluk rakus mirip domba dengan taring besar, dan ada pula yang menggambarkannya sebagai pekari besar pemakan daging.
long_description.en: Ao Ao is a monstrous creature of South American mythology, one of the cursed sons of Tau and Kerana and one of the central mythological creatures among Guarani-speaking cultures. A museum source in Paraguay calls it the sixth son of Tau and Kerana. It is often described as a voracious sheep-like creature with huge fangs, while others describe it as a large, carnivorous peccary.

long_description.id: Menurut cerita, hewan ini melahap tanpa belas kasihan siapa pun yang berjalan di hutan; ia dikatakan hanya makan manusia. Seseorang dapat selamat jika berhasil memanjat pohon pindó, palem yang dianggap tanaman suci dan selalu dipakai pada Pekan Suci. Dalam sebagian versi, Ao Ao menyantap anak-anak yang tidak patuh yang dibawakan saudaranya, Jasy Jatere, dan di Paraguay orang dewasa menakut-nakuti anak dengan mengatakan Ao Ao akan datang.
long_description.en: In the tales, this animal mercilessly devours anyone walking in the woods; it is said to have people as its sole food. A person can survive by climbing a pindó, a palm regarded as a sacred plant and always used in Holy Week. In some versions Ao Ao feasts on disobedient children brought by its brother Jasy Jatere, and in Paraguay adults frighten children by saying that Ao Ao will come.

long_description.id: Ao Ao dipercaya hidup di pegunungan dan hutan lebat, dan keturunannya yang banyak dan dikutuk dengan cara yang sama disebut menjadi penguasa dan pelindung bukit serta gunung. Sumber museum itu juga menyebutnya dewa kesuburan, dan penutur lisan mitologi Guarani menegaskan bahwa semua anaknya kanibal dan ganas. Di daerah Mbuyapey ia disebut Ovecha Ka'aguy karena sangat mirip domba. Namanya berasal dari bunyi lolongannya, "Ao ao ao!", saat mengejar korban.
long_description.en: Ao Ao is believed to have lived in the sierras and dense forests, and its many offspring, cursed in the same manner, are said to have served as lords and protectors of the hills and mountains. The museum source also calls it the god of fertility, and oral transmitters of Guarani mythology assert that all its children are cannibals and fierce. In the Mbuyapey area it was called Ovecha Ka'aguy because it closely resembles a sheep. Its name comes from the sound of its howl, "Ao ao ao!", when pursuing victims.

description.id: Menurut cerita, korban yang berhasil memanjat pohon pindó dapat menyelamatkan nyawanya.
description.en: According to the tale, a victim who manages to climb a pindó palm can save his life.

note.en: In some versions, Jasy Jatere brings disobedient children to Ao Ao.

short_description.id: Aonyōbō adalah yōkai Jepang berkulit biru yang menyerupai perempuan bangsawan istana zaman dahulu dan dikaitkan dengan rumah-rumah bangsawan yang runtuh.
short_description.en: Aonyōbō is a blue-skinned Japanese yōkai resembling an ancient court noblewoman, associated with the abandoned homes of fallen nobles.

long_description.id: Aonyōbō (青女房) adalah yōkai dalam mitologi Jepang. Ia digambarkan sebagai roh seperti ogre berkulit biru yang membawa kemiskinan dan kemalangan, dan tampil sebagai perempuan bangsawan istana zaman kuno.
long_description.en: Aonyōbō (青女房) is a yōkai in Japanese mythology. It is described as a blue-skinned, ogre-like spirit of poverty and misfortune that takes the appearance of an ancient court noblewoman.

long_description.id: Ia berpakaian banyak kimono dari zaman lampau yang kini compang-camping dan dimakan ngengat, dengan wajah putih ala bangsawan istana kuno, beralis tinggi, dan bergigi hitam. Ia tinggal di rumah-rumah terbengkalai bekas kediaman bangsawan yang jatuh, terus berdandan dan merapikan penampilan menanti tamu yang tak kunjung datang.
long_description.en: Her layered robes belong to earlier ages and have turned ragged and moth-eaten, and her face is painted white in the manner of old-time courtiers, with raised painted eyebrows and blackened teeth. She dwells in empty houses once held by ruined noble families, forever applying cosmetics and fixing her hair for visitors who never come.

long_description.id: Kamus digital Jepang menggambarkannya sebagai yōkai berwujud perempuan berdandan yang tinggal di rumah di tengah rumpun bambu yang terbengkalai, dan menyebut nama lainnya, 青女.
long_description.en: A Japanese digital dictionary describes it as a yōkai in the form of a made-up woman living in a house within a ruined bamboo grove, and gives the alternative name 青女.

literal_meaning.id: Kata ini dalam kamus berarti perempuan muda yang belum berpengalaman yang melayani di istana atau rumah bangsawan, atau perempuan berstatus rendah.
literal_meaning.en: In dictionaries the word means a young, inexperienced woman serving at court or in a noble household, or a woman of low status.

short_description.id: Apalpador adalah raksasa pembuat arang dari tradisi Natal Galisia yang turun dari pegunungan pada malam Natal atau Tahun Baru untuk meraba perut anak-anak dan meninggalkan kastanye.
short_description.en: The Apalpador is a giant charcoal-burner of Galician Christmas tradition who comes down from the mountains on Christmas or New Year's Eve to feel children's bellies and leave chestnuts.

long_description.id: Apalpador, Apalpabarrigas, atau Pandigueiro adalah raksasa pembuat arang berpakaian compang-camping yang tinggal di pegunungan Galisia timur seperti Courel dan Terra de Trives. Pada malam Natal atau Tahun Baru ia turun dan masuk ke rumah, meraba perut anak-anak untuk melihat apakah mereka makan cukup, lalu meninggalkan kastanye, kadang hadiah, dan mendoakan tahun yang penuh makanan. Malam itu disebut noite de apalpadoiro, dan ada pula versi perempuannya, Pandigueira.
long_description.en: The Apalpador, Apalpabarrigas or Pandigueiro is a ragged giant charcoal-burner who lives in the eastern Galician mountains such as Courel and Terra de Trives. On Christmas or New Year's Eve he comes down and enters houses, feels children's bellies to see if they have eaten enough, then leaves chestnuts, sometimes a present, and wishes them a year full of food. The night is called noite de apalpadoiro, and there is also a female version, the Pandigueira.

long_description.id: Lagu-lagu rakyat tentangnya dinyanyikan untuk menyuruh anak-anak tidur. Sejak 2006 tokoh ini dihidupkan kembali oleh José André Lôpez Gonçâlez dan perkumpulan A Gentalha do Pichel sebagai tokoh Natal Galisia.
long_description.en: Folk songs about him are sung to send children to bed. Since 2006 he has been revived by José André Lôpez Gonçâlez and the association A Gentalha do Pichel as a Galician Christmas figure.

statement.en: He is a ragged charcoal-burner who on Christmas Eve or New Year's Eve enters houses, feels the children's bellies and, if they are not full, leaves a handful of chestnuts; the rest of the year he lives in the eastern mountains of Galicia.

short_description.id: Ardov adalah roh atau jin air dalam mitologi Turk yang diyakini tinggal di sumber-sumber air dan tidak mencelakai manusia.
short_description.en: Ardov is a water spirit or water jinn of Turkic mythology, believed to live at water sources and to do no harm to people.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Turk, Ardov dikenal sebagai jin air (su cini), dan satu kamus mitologi menyebutnya makhluk yang mewakili roh air. Nama lainnya antara lain Ardoy, Erdov, Erdoy, dan Ardoğ. Menurut kepercayaan, ia menghuni sumber-sumber air dan tidak berbahaya bagi manusia.
long_description.en: In Turkic mythology Ardov is known as a water jinn (su cini), and one mythology dictionary describes it as a being that represents the water spirit. Other names include Ardoy, Erdov, Erdoy and Ardoğ. According to belief it dwells at water sources and is harmless to people.

long_description.id: Ardov digambarkan sebagai perempuan jangkung berambut pirang yang sangat cantik. Pada malam hari ia membawa lari kuda dan memacunya sampai pagi hingga kuda itu basah oleh keringat. Bila terdesak, ia masuk ke sumur atau sungai kecil lalu menghilang.
long_description.en: Ardov is described as a tall, fair-haired and very beautiful woman. At night it carries off horses and rides them until morning, leaving them drenched in sweat. When cornered it slips into a well or a stream and vanishes.

long_description.id: Untuk menjauhkannya, ketika seseorang dimakamkan, lampu atau cahaya dinyalakan di kepala makam selama tiga hari. Ardov dibandingkan dengan Vudaş (Vutaş) dalam mitologi Chuvash, dan sebuah sumber juga menyebut makhluk Artavaz dari kepercayaan Tatar, meski hubungannya belum jelas.
long_description.en: To keep it away, a light is kept burning at the head of a grave for three days after a burial. Ardov is compared with Vudaş (Vutaş) of Chuvash mythology, and one source also mentions a being called Artavaz in Tatar folk belief, although the link is not settled.

short_description.id: Arganão adalah makhluk ladang dari tradisi lisan Melgaço, Portugal, yang diam-diam mengamati dan menjahili manusia tanpa pernah terlihat.
short_description.en: The arganão is a field being of the oral tradition of Melgaço, Portugal, that secretly watches and pranks people without ever being seen.

long_description.id: Arganão adalah tokoh mitis dari tradisi lisan Melgaço di Portugal utara. Ia tinggal di ladang tetapi sangat penasaran pada kehidupan manusia dan menghabiskan hari dengan diam-diam mengamati mereka. Ia hampir tak terlihat, terhibur oleh tingkah manusia, dan sesekali menjahili atau mengagetkan mereka tanpa pernah tertangkap. Kisahnya tidak tercatat dalam dokumen sebelum awal abad ke-20.
long_description.en: The arganão is a mythical figure from the oral tradition of Melgaço in northern Portugal. He lives in the fields but is intensely curious about human life and spends his days secretly watching people. He is almost invisible, amused by human behaviour, and occasionally plays pranks or gives small frights without ever being caught. His stories are not recorded in documents before the early 20th century.

long_description.id: Artikel berbahasa Portugis mencatat adanya proyek budaya untuk menghidupkan kembali tradisi ini, yang diduga berasal dari tradisi pagan. Tersebar anggapan keliru bahwa sosok berkaki empat pada relief tinggi di Igreja Matriz de Melgaço adalah arganão; menurut tafsiran Carlos Alberto Ferreira de Almeida, itu canid penjaga yang garang atau serigala. Arganão menjadi tokoh utama arak-arakan etnografis "Melgaço em Festa" tahun 2017, dan pada 2013 kelompok teater Comédias do Minho membawakan pertunjukan jalanan "Arganão" untuk siswa di Monção.
long_description.en: The Portuguese article records cultural projects to revive the tradition, which is presumed to be of pagan origin. A version wrongly spread that the four-legged figure in high relief at the Igreja Matriz de Melgaço is an arganão; according to Carlos Alberto Ferreira de Almeida's interpretation it is a fierce guard canid or a wolf. The arganões were the central figure of the 2017 'Melgaço em Festa' ethnographic parade, and in 2013 the theatre company Comédias do Minho presented a street performance, 'Arganão', to pupils in Monção.

selection_criteria: computeFillStatus must be lengkap-informasi: complete, valid research without an approved image.
No active editorial artwork and no permanent artwork exclusion.
The accepted research entry is embedded unchanged; the image may only depict what its claims document.
Creatures an earlier batch left out keep that reason as catatan_sebelumnya; the generator may decline them with status tidak-digambar.

user_policy.name: sangar
user_policy.intent: Every illustration must feel 'sangar': dangerous, imposing or awe-inspiring, with the being as the undeniable subject. The owner rejected earlier images that read as an ordinary person, an ordinary animal, an empty landscape, or a calm, cute or decorative portrait. Those outcomes are failures regardless of technical quality.
user_policy.subject: The being dominates the frame and is clearly the subject. Head, eyes and distinguishing traits are readable even at thumbnail size. Never a landscape without the being, never a human who could be a passer-by, never a farm animal at pasture.
user_policy.moment: Depict a moment, not a pose: hunting, emerging, striking, commanding, towering, descending, tearing through weather or ground. Gaze and posture confront or loom over the viewer. Standing still and facing the camera with a neutral expression is not acceptable.
user_policy.effects: Visible power is wanted and may be strong, but every effect must come from a power, domain, attribute, habitat or deed documented in the research claims of that being, and it must act physically on the world: ground cracking, water rearing, trees bending, lightning striking, flame consuming, fog pouring, bodies of victims turned to stone. No generic glowing envelope, neon outline, energy ribbons, floating runes or luminous coloured mist. If the research documents no power, build menace from anatomy, scale, moment, light and setting instead, and record that in artistic_choices.
user_policy.fidelity: Anatomy, attributes, number of heads, eyes, limbs and iconography follow the research claims exactly. Effects and atmosphere add power; they never replace or invent anatomy. Fully opaque clothing where a humanlike form is clothed; no nudity, no explicit gore.
user_policy.composition: Low camera angle; monumental or predatory scale with small environmental references when size is documented, otherwise dominance through tight framing and foreshortening. Strong silhouette, high contrast, cinematic low-key lighting from one dominant source (moon, fire, lightning, dying sun), rim light, dust, smoke, rain or spray. Tactile surfaces: wet scales, matted fur, cracked skin, rust, weathered cloth, stone.
user_policy.setting: The place its stories name: graveyard, swamp, sea cliff, battlefield, celestial palace, desert storm. Weather and time of day heighten threat or majesty. Palette is dark and warm with one strong accent, consistent with the collection; no pastel, no flat even daylight.
user_policy.respect: Living religions (Hindu, Buddhist, Shinto, Abrahamic and folk deities still worshipped) are majestic and overwhelming rather than monstrous: cosmic scale, divine radiance from documented attributes, the elements they rule in motion. Malevolent beings are menacing. Literary beings follow their source text, never a film, game, anime or comic design.
user_policy.aniconic: If the research documents no bodily form at all, either depict the documented manifestation as an active, overwhelming force (the sky itself splitting, a storm swallowing the steppe) with the choice recorded in artistic_choices, or decline the entry with status tidak-digambar. A calm scene without agency fails.
user_policy.self_check: Before accepting an image the generator answers all of these with yes: the being dominates the frame; it still looks dangerous or majestic at 200 px; there is a moment, not a static pose; each visible effect points to a claim id; head, eye and limb counts match the claims; no text, watermark, border or borrowed design; it would not be rejected as ordinary person, ordinary animal, landscape only, or cute and calm. One no means regenerate, keep the rejected attempt as history, up to three attempts.
user_policy.style: Square premium painterly cinematic illustration in the house style of the existing artwork, more dramatic and higher contrast. No text, labels, logo, border or watermark.
user_policy.sources: Never copy designs from films, games, anime or comics (modern_depictions). Every design is original and sourced from the accepted research.
